chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Sulaym al-Farra', from the one who informed him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
'Arabise the Quran, for indeed it is Arabic.'

key_terms.أَعْرِبِ: Arabise — imperative from أَعْرَبَ, meaning to speak or pronounce clearly in Arabic, to articulate with correct Arabic phonetics and grammar
key_terms.عَرَبِيٌّ: Arabic — the Quran is intrinsically an Arabic text; reciting it in proper Arabic is thus essential to its nature

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about reciting the Quran in Arabic?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) instructs believers to recite the Quran with correct and clear Arabic pronunciation, giving as the reason that the Quran itself is an Arabic scripture. This teaching was directed at a community in which Persian and other non-Arab linguistic influences were widespread, reminding them that the Quran's sanctity is inseparable from its Arabic form. The imperative أَعْرِبِ (i'rib) implies both proper phonetic articulation and grammatical precision in recitation.
word_analysis: articulate in Arabic/recite with proper Arabic
